mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST increases over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period indicates strong consumer demand and a robust labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a potential deflationary pressure, which increases real interest rates and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals an economic contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 1% in a quarter.
